_meta.source: Written for claudeDM (Sci-Fi category). Mostly original; a few general-mechanics sentences (e.g. opportunity attacks, passive checks, stat-block phrasing) are adapted from SRD 5.1, licensed CC BY 4.0 — see NOTICE.
_meta.notes: Six abilities and the 18 Sci-Fi skills. Use ONLY these skill names on Sci-Fi character sheets. Same ability modifier, passive check and DC rules as the shared d20 chassis.

abilities.name: Strength
abilities.description: Strength is raw physical power: muscle, leverage and the ability to apply force. Use it to force a jammed hatch, haul a wounded teammate out of a firefight, swing a fire axe or keep a grip on a speeding car's roof.
common_uses: Carrying capacity and dragging bodies or gear
Meeting the Strength requirement of heavy armor

abilities.name: Dexterity
abilities.description: Dexterity covers hand-eye coordination, reflexes and balance. It is the gunfighter's ability: every firearm, energy weapon and thrown grenade is aimed with it, and it governs how fast you react when the shooting starts.
common_uses: Ranged attack rolls with all firearms and energy weapons
Damage on single shots with Sidearms, Longarms and Automatics
Armor Class in light and medium armor
Dodging blasts and full-auto fire (DEX saves)

abilities.name: Constitution
abilities.description: Constitution is toughness, stamina and the body's ability to absorb punishment: gunshot trauma, toxins, sleep deprivation, vacuum exposure and the after-effects of combat stims.
common_uses: Resisting stun guns, flashbangs, gas and toxins
Holding your breath, marching without rest

abilities.name: Intelligence
abilities.description: Intelligence is reasoning, memory and technical education. It covers breaking into networks, fixing an engine under fire, analyzing a crime scene and understanding what the alien specimen on the table actually is.

abilities.name: Wisdom
abilities.description: Wisdom is awareness, intuition and judgment. It lets you spot the sniper on the rooftop, read whether the fixer is lying, keep your nerve under suppressive fire and find your way through a city or a wilderness you don't know.
common_uses: Resisting suppression, fear and shock (WIS saves)

abilities.name: Charisma
abilities.description: Charisma is force of personality: confidence, charm, presence and the ability to make people believe you. A high-Charisma character talks past checkpoints, bluffs a gang into backing down and keeps a frightened squad together.

skills.name: Acrobatics
skills.description: Keeping your balance and moving with agility: vaulting a fence mid-chase, rolling out of a moving vehicle, crossing a narrow ledge, slipping out of a grapple or keeping your footing on a pitching deck.

skills.name: Athletics
skills.description: Climbing, jumping, swimming, sprinting while carrying gear and wrestling. Use it to scale a chain-link fence, kick in a door, grapple a suspect or win a foot chase through a crowded market.

skills.name: Computers
skills.description: Operating, programming and breaking into computer systems, networks, phones and electronic locks. Covers hacking, data recovery, tracing a signal and erasing your tracks. DC 10 consumer device, 15 corporate or police system, 20 military, 25 state-of-the-art or alien. In the 1980s this means terminals, modems, phone lines and magnetic tape.

skills.name: Deception
skills.description: Convincingly hiding the truth: lying to a guard, keeping a cover story straight under questioning, bluffing about the size of your backup, or passing a forged badge with a straight face.

skills.name: Insight
skills.description: Reading people: spotting a lie, sensing nervousness, guessing someone's next move from their body language or noticing that the informant is more afraid of someone else than of you.

skills.name: Intimidation
skills.description: Getting what you want through threats, menace or a display of force: making a thug back off, scaring a witness into talking or staring down a checkpoint.

skills.name: Investigation
skills.description: Searching for clues and drawing conclusions: working a crime scene, following a paper trail, finding the hidden compartment, reconstructing a firefight from shell casings or spotting the weak point in a security plan.

skills.name: Mechanics
skills.description: Building, repairing, sabotaging and bypassing machines and hardware: engines, weapons, locks, alarms, drones, robots and starship systems. Clearing a stubborn jam out of combat, hot-wiring a car or rigging a booby trap all use Mechanics.

skills.name: Medicine
skills.description: First aid, trauma care and diagnosis. Stabilize a dying ally (DC 10), stop bleeding, identify a toxin or infection, judge the time of death or tell whether a wound came from a knife or a laser.

skills.name: Perception
skills.description: Using your senses to notice things: the glint of a scope, the footsteps behind you, the tripwire across the doorway, the tail two cars back. Passive Perception is how alert you are when not actively looking.

skills.name: Performance
skills.description: Entertaining or holding an audience: music, acting, public speaking, a convincing cover identity at a party, or a distraction loud enough to pull the guards away.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.description: Influencing people honestly through tact, reasoning and goodwill: negotiating a deal, calming a hostage-taker, recruiting an ally or talking a cop into letting you go with a warning.

skills.name: Piloting
skills.description: Driving and flying vehicles under pressure: cars, motorcycles, boats, helicopters and spacecraft. Used for chases, evasive maneuvers, ramming, landing a damaged craft and docking in zero gravity.

skills.name: Science
skills.description: Knowledge of physics, chemistry, biology, astronomy and engineering theory. Identify a chemical, understand an experiment, analyze an alien organism, calculate an orbit or recognize what a strange signal means.

skills.name: Sleight of Hand
skills.description: Manual trickery: picking a pocket, palming a data chip, planting a bug, concealing a holdout pistol from a pat-down or swapping a real document for a forgery.

skills.name: Stealth
skills.description: Moving unseen and unheard: sneaking past a patrol, tailing a target, slipping through a dark warehouse or lying still while the hunter passes.

skills.name: Streetwise
skills.description: Knowing how the street works: finding a fence, a doctor who won't ask questions or a black-market arms dealer; reading gang colors and territory; hearing rumors; knowing which neighborhoods to avoid after dark.

skills.name: Survival
skills.description: Living off the land and finding your way: tracking, hunting, navigating without GPS, predicting weather, finding shelter and clean water, and reading the signs that something dangerous has passed this way.

ability_score_modifiers.description: To find an ability modifier, subtract 10 from the score, divide by 2 and round down.

passive_checks.description: A passive check is a check made without rolling, representing a character's steady, background level of competence (for example, noticing an ambush while walking a patrol route). The GM uses it to decide secretly whether a character notices or achieves something.
passive_checks.formula: 10 + all modifiers that normally apply to the check. If the character has advantage on the check, add 5. For disadvantage, subtract 5.
